text: A worker claims a background job using a lease token. An expired lease allows crash recovery. A stale worker cannot acknowledge a job after its lease expires.
Failed background jobs retry with exponential backoff. Exhausted attempts enter a dead letter state. Operators can inspect error events and retry dead jobs manually.
An idempotency key deduplicates repeated API submissions. A matching payload returns the existing job. Reusing a key with a different payload returns a conflict.
SQLite immediate transactions serialize writers. A transaction atomically selects and updates a job. WAL permits readers while another connection writes.
Evaluate search ranking with recall, mean reciprocal rank and normalized discounted cumulative gain. Relevance judgments assign graded labels to query document pairs.
BM25 is a lexical search ranking function with term frequency saturation and document length normalization. Inverse document frequency downweights common terms.
TF-IDF weights words using term frequency and inverse document frequency. Cosine similarity compares query vectors to document vectors in a shared vocabulary.
Keep cloud credentials out of version control. Use a secret manager and restrict service permissions. Rotate credentials when exposed and avoid logging access tokens.
A container filesystem is ephemeral. Persist durable application state on a volume. SQLite requires a local filesystem rather than a shared network filesystem for WAL.
An accessible frontend uses semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, visible focus, labels and status announcements. Error messages should help users recover.
A HAR capture records HTTP requests and latency. Aggregate API routes and inspect p50 and p95 latency, failed requests and sample counts before setting performance budgets.

Lexical retrieval cannot reliably match synonyms without overlapping terms. A semantic embedding retriever is a useful comparison baseline. Tune on development queries and reserve a held out test set.
